Vendor learning path

Manhattan Active platform: Omni, Warehouse Management, Transportation Management

Manhattan focuses on supply chain execution and omnichannel commerce. Manhattan Active Omni handles order management, store fulfilment and customer service; Manhattan Active Warehouse Management runs DCs with order streaming and built-in WES; Manhattan Active Transportation Management covers freight. It sits next to an ERP, not in place of one.

OMSWMSTMS

Learning path

Foundations

Beginner / BA
  • Why retailers use a dedicated OMS and WMS next to ERP
  • Order lifecycle in Active Omni: capture → availability → allocate → release → fulfil
  • Inside a DC: receiving to shipping
  • Order streaming vs fixed waves

Exercise. Explain to a store manager how a ship-from-store order reaches their team.

Functional

Consultant
  • Sourcing and allocation rule design: distance, cost, capacity, protection rules
  • Fulfilment options: ship, BOPIS, ship-from-store, same-day
  • Order states, holds and exception handling
  • WMS: location setup, putaway, allocation, order streaming, cartonisation
  • Labour and automation in the warehouse

Exercise. Design sourcing rules where stores fulfil only when DCs cannot meet the promise date.

Technical

Developer / Data
  • REST APIs and messaging for orders, inventory and shipments
  • Inventory feeds from ERP, POS and WMS: full sync vs deltas
  • Shipment confirmation back to OMS and ERP
  • Extending a versionless platform: configuration over customisation

Exercise. Design the inventory sync that keeps store availability fresh within 60 seconds.

Architecture

Architect
  • OMS as owner of the promise; ERP as owner of finance
  • Peak scaling for sale events
  • Store connectivity and offline behaviour
  • Coexistence with SAP or Oracle ERP

Exercise. Draw the Manhattan Omni + WM ↔ SAP S/4HANA flow (see integration scenarios).

Same concept, Manhattan Associates vocabulary

Generic termManhattan Associates
OMSManhattan Active Omni (order management)
Network availabilityInventory availability across DCs and stores
SourcingConfigurable sourcing / allocation rules
Wave planningWaves and order streaming (waveless)
Automation orchestrationBuilt-in warehouse execution (WES)
Store fulfilmentStore fulfilment within Active Omni
Release modelCloud-native, versionless, continuously updated

Use cases

Ship-from-store for an apparel retailer

Online demand peaks while DC capacity is fixed.

Active Omni treats stores as fulfilment nodes with capacity limits and protection stock; orders route to stores when they can meet the promise; staff pick with a store app.

KPIs: Store fulfilment rate · cancellations due to short picks · markdown reduction

Peak-season DC throughput

Same-day orders with tight carrier cut-offs.

Order streaming releases work continuously by due time alongside waves for store replenishment; WES coordinates robots and pickers.

KPIs: Units per hour · cut-off adherence

Integration surface

API-first, cloud-native microservices on the Manhattan Active platform; REST APIs and messaging for orders, inventory, ASNs and shipment confirmations; versionless continuous updates.

Product names and modules evolve. Verify against current Manhattan Associates documentation.
